title: Impact of Vietnam Service on Long-Term Earnings

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Method: Instrumental Variables (IV) / Two-Stage Least Squares (2SLS)**

**Rationale:** Military service during Vietnam is endogenous — volunteers differ systematically from non-volunteers in ways correlated with earnings (motivation, health, risk preferences, etc.). OLS estimates of the effect of service on earnings will be biased.

The **draft lottery number** (z) provides a natural experiment: lottery numbers were randomly assigned, creating exogenous variation in the probability of serving. This is the classic Angrist (1990) design.

**Key assumptions:**
1. **Relevance:** The draft lottery number (z) must be correlated with actual Vietnam service (x). We test this via the first-stage F-statistic.
2. **Independence/Exogeneity:** The lottery number is randomly assigned, so it should be uncorrelated with potential outcomes (and any unobserved determinants of earnings). This is satisfied by design.
3. **Exclusion Restriction:** The draft lottery number affects earnings *only* through its effect on military service, not through any other channel.
4. **Monotonicity:** Having a low (draft-eligible) lottery number makes service weakly more likely for everyone (no "defiers").

The IV estimate recovers the **Local Average Treatment Effect (LATE)** — the causal effect of Vietnam service on earnings for compliers (those whose service status was changed by their lottery number).

## 2. R Code

```r
# ============================================================
# IV Analysis: Impact of Vietnam Service on Long-Term Earnings
# Instrument: Draft Lottery Number
# ============================================================

# Load required packages
if (!require("AER")) install.packages("AER", repos="http://cran.r-project.org")
if (!require("lmtest")) install.packages("lmtest", repos="http://cran.r-project.org")
if (!require("sandwich")) install.packages("sandwich", repos="http://cran.r-project.org")

library(AER)
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load and inspect data
# --------------------------------------------------
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s69_data.csv")
cat("=== Data Summary ===\n")
cat("Observations:", nrow(df), "\n")
cat("Columns:", names(df), "\n\n")
summary(df)
cat("\n")

# Check correlation between instrument and endogenous variable
cat("=== Correlation: z and x ===\n")
cat("Cor(z, x):", round(cor(df$z, df$x), 4), "\n")
cat("Cor(z, y):", round(cor(df$z, df$y), 4), "\n")
cat("Cor(x, y):", round(cor(df$x, df$y), 4), "\n\n")

# --------------------------------------------------
# 2. OLS (Naive) Estimation
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("========================================\n")
cat("=== OLS: Naive Regression (Biased) ===\n")
cat("========================================\n")
ols_no_ctrl <- lm(y ~ x, data = df)
ols_with_ctrl <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = df)

cat("\nOLS without controls:\n")
print(coeftest(ols_no_ctrl, vcov = vcovHC(ols_no_ctrl, type = "HC1")))

cat("\nOLS with controls:\n")
print(coeftest(ols_with_ctrl, vcov = vcovHC(ols_with_ctrl, type = "HC1")))

# --------------------------------------------------
# 3. First Stage: z -> x
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("=== First Stage: z -> x ===\n")
cat("========================================\n")

first_stage <- lm(x ~ z, data = df)
first_stage_ctrl <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = df)

cat("\nFirst stage without controls:\n")
print(coeftest(first_stage, vcov = vcovHC(first_stage, type = "HC1")))

# F-statistic for instrument strength
fs_summary <- summary(first_stage)
cat("\nFirst-stage F-statistic (no controls):", 
    round(fs_summary$fstatistic[1], 2), "\n")

fs_summary_ctrl <- summary(first_stage_ctrl)
cat("First-stage F-statistic (with controls):", 
    round(fs_summary_ctrl$fstatistic[1], 2), "\n")

# Rule of thumb: F > 10 for strong instrument
cat("Instrument strength: ", 
    ifelse(fs_summary$fstatistic[1] > 10, "STRONG (F > 10)", "WEAK (F <= 10)"), "\n\n")

# --------------------------------------------------
# 4. Reduced Form: z -> y
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("========================================\n")
cat("=== Reduced Form: z -> y ===\n")
cat("========================================\n")
reduced_form <- lm(y ~ z, data = df)
reduced_form_ctrl <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = df)

cat("\nReduced form without controls:\n")
print(coeftest(reduced_form, vcov = vcovHC(reduced_form, type = "HC1")))

cat("\nReduced form with controls:\n")
print(coeftest(reduced_form_ctrl, vcov = vcovHC(reduced_form_ctrl, type = "HC1")))

# --------------------------------------------------
# 5. IV / 2SLS Estimation (Main Results)
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("=== IV/2SLS: Main Results ===\n")
cat("========================================\n")

# IV without controls
iv_no_ctrl <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = df)
cat("\n--- IV without controls ---\n")
print(coeftest(iv_no_ctrl, vcov = vcovHC(iv_no_ctrl, type = "HC1")))

# IV with controls
iv_with_ctrl <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = df)
cat("\n--- IV with controls ---\n")
print(coeftest(iv_with_ctrl, vcov = vcovHC(iv_with_ctrl, type = "HC1")))

# Wald estimator (manual check): reduced form / first stage
wald_est <- coef(reduced_form)["z"] / coef(first_stage)["z"]
cat("\n--- Manual Wald Estimate (RF/FS) ---\n")
cat("Wald IV estimate:", round(wald_est, 4), "\n")
cat("2SLS estimate:   ", round(coef(iv_no_ctrl)["x"], 4), "\n")

# --------------------------------------------------
# 6. Diagnostic Tests
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("=== Diagnostic Tests ===\n")
cat("========================================\n")

# Hausman test: compare OLS vs IV
cat("\n--- Hausman-type endogeneity test ---\n")
# Manual Hausman: add first-stage residuals to OLS
df$fs_resid <- residuals(first_stage)
hausman_reg <- lm(y ~ x + fs_resid, data = df)
hausman_pval <- coeftest(hausman_reg)["fs_resid", "Pr(>|t|)"]
cat("Coefficient on first-stage residuals:", 
    round(coef(hausman_reg)["fs_resid"], 4), "\n")
cat("p-value:", round(hausman_pval, 4), "\n")
cat("Endogeneity:", ifelse(hausman_pval < 0.05, 
    "REJECTED exogeneity of x (IV preferred)", 
    "Cannot reject exogeneity of x"), "\n")

# Instrument validity: check z is uncorrelated with controls (balance test)
cat("\n--- Balance Test: z vs controls ---\n")
balance_test <- lm(controls ~ z, data = df)
balance_coef <- coeftest(balance_test)
print(balance_coef)
cat("Balance check p-value:", round(balance_coef["z", "Pr(>|t|)"], 4), "\n")
cat("Balance:", ifelse(balance_coef["z", "Pr(>|t|)"] > 0.05, 
    "PASS (z uncorrelated with controls)", 
    "CONCERN (z correlated with controls)"), "\n")

# --------------------------------------------------
# 7. Robustness Checks
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("=== Robustness Checks ===\n")
cat("========================================\n")

# A. Subsample analysis by control variable median split
med_ctrl <- median(df$controls)
df$high_ctrl <- as.integer(df$controls > med_ctrl)

cat("\n--- Subsample: Below median controls ---\n")
iv_low <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = df[df$high_ctrl == 0, ])
print(coeftest(iv_low, vcov = vcovHC(iv_low, type = "HC1")))

cat("\n--- Subsample: Above median controls ---\n")
iv_high <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = df[df$high_ctrl == 1, ])
print(coeftest(iv_high, vcov = vcovHC(iv_high, type = "HC1")))

# B. Interaction specification
cat("\n--- IV with interaction (x * controls) ---\n")
iv_interact <- ivreg(y ~ x * controls | z * controls, data = df)
print(coeftest(iv_interact, vcov = vcovHC(iv_interact, type = "HC1")))

# --------------------------------------------------
# 8. Summary Table
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("=== SUMMARY OF KEY RESULTS ===\n")
cat("========================================\n\n")

ols_coef <- coef(ols_no_ctrl)["x"]
ols_se <- coeftest(ols_no_ctrl, vcov = vcovHC(ols_no_ctrl, type = "HC1"))["x", "Std. Error"]
iv_coef <- coef(iv_no_ctrl)["x"]
iv_se <- coeftest(iv_no_ctrl, vcov = vcovHC(iv_no_ctrl, type = "HC1"))["x", "Std. Error"]
iv_ctrl_coef <- coef(iv_with_ctrl)["x"]
iv_ctrl_se <- coeftest(iv_with_ctrl, vcov = vcovHC(iv_with_ctrl, type = "HC1"))["x", "Std. Error"]

cat(sprintf("%-30s %10s %10s\n", "Model", "Coef(x)", "Robust SE"))
cat(paste(rep("-", 52), collapse=""), "\n")
cat(sprintf("%-30s %10.4f %10.4f\n", "OLS (no controls)", ols_coef, ols_se))
cat(sprintf("%-30s %10.4f %10.4f\n", "OLS (with controls)", 
    coef(ols_with_ctrl)["x"], 
    coeftest(ols_with_ctrl, vcov = vcovHC(ols_with_ctrl, type = "HC1"))["x", "Std. Error"]))
cat(sprintf("%-30s %10.4f %10.4f\n", "IV/2SLS (no controls)", iv_coef, iv_se))
cat(sprintf("%-30s %10.4f %10.4f\n", "IV/2SLS (with controls)", iv_ctrl_coef, iv_ctrl_se))
cat(paste(rep("-", 52), collapse=""), "\n")
cat(sprintf("%-30s %10.2f\n", "First-stage F-stat", fs_summary$fstatistic[1]))
cat(sprintf("%-30s %10d\n", "N", nrow(df)))

cat("\n=== MAIN FINDING ===\n")
cat(sprintf("The IV estimate of the effect of Vietnam service on log earnings is %.4f\n", iv_coef))
cat(sprintf("This implies a %.1f%% change in earnings due to military service.\n", 
    (exp(iv_coef) - 1) * 100))
cat(sprintf("(Robust SE: %.4f, 95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f])\n", 
    iv_se, iv_coef - 1.96*iv_se, iv_coef + 1.96*iv_se))
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Expected sign: Negative.** Based on the seminal Angrist (1990) study and subsequent literature:

- **IV estimate of Vietnam service on log earnings:** Expected to be **negative**, likely in the range of **-0.10 to -0.30** (i.e., a 10-25% earnings penalty). Angrist (1990) found approximately a 15% reduction in earnings for white veterans.

- **OLS vs IV comparison:** The OLS estimate may be **attenuated toward zero or even positive** due to selection bias — men who served may have had certain characteristics (discipline, health) that positively affect earnings, partially offsetting the negative causal effect of service disruption.

- **First stage:** The draft lottery number (z) should be a strong predictor of service (x), with an F-statistic well above 10, since the lottery directly determined draft eligibility.

- **Mechanism:** The earnings penalty likely operates through **disrupted human capital accumulation** — time spent in military service displaced years of education and labor market experience during a critical period.

- **Reduced form:** The coefficient of z on y should be negative but smaller in magnitude than the IV estimate, since the lottery affected only a fraction of those drafted (first-stage coefficient < 1).

- **Balance test:** The lottery number should be uncorrelated with pre-determined controls (age, education measured pre-lottery), confirming the instrument's validity.

The exact magnitudes will depend on this particular simulation's data-generating process, but the qualitative patterns should align with the Angrist (1990) framework.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use draft lottery number as an instrument for Vietnam service.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Military service during the Vietnam War positively affects long-term earnings.
